question.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x=\{7,\,2,\,12\},\,y=\{-1,\,9,\,7\}
$$

You're given that $\overset{―}{x}=7,$ $\overset{―}{y}=5,$ ${\sigma }_{x}≈4.082,$ and ${\sigma }_{y}≈4.320.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The (population) linear correlation coefficient of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\rho (x,y)=\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}
$$

where $\text{Cov}(x,y)$ is the covariance, and ${\sigma }_{x}$ and ${\sigma }_{y}$ are the standard deviations of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the covariance:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(7-7)(-1-5)+(2-7)(9-5)+(12-7)(7-5)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(0)(-6)+(-5)(4)+(5)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[0-20+10] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-10) \\  & ≈-3.333\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the formula. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}} \\  & ≈\frac{(-3.333)}{4.082\cdot 4.320} \\  & ≈-0.19\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
